## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A

response.rationale: These are probably two related concepts, not one. "Skate Hire" in BookingService (3aa201f0edaa9fd6, src/business/bookingService.ts) is the act of hiring skates in a size as part of a booking. Hiring fails when no skates of that size are left: `if (this.stock.get(size) === 0) throw new DomainError(400, `no hire skates of size ${size}`);`. "Hire Skate Stock" in HireStockRepository (ada57feca2e90c67, src/persistence/hireStockRepository.ts) is the stock of hire skates, counted per size: `private readonly stock = new Map<string, number>();`. So the booking side checks the stock, and the stock is a separate thing that SessionService.availability also reads. Hiring skates out and holding a stock of skates are different real-world things, so A and B don't model the same concept.
